title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Jewellery pays the rent, watches anchor the heritage, eyewear builds clinical trust, and emerging brands buy tomorrow's optionality.
epigraph.author: Structural anatomy of Titan's portfolio

web_blocks.html: Titan operates four primary verticals: Jewellery, Watches & Wearables, EyeCare, and Emerging Businesses plus TEAL [1][4]. It also runs international retail across the GCC, North America, and Singapore. In FY26, audited consolidated revenue reached ₹87,584 crore, including ₹12,058 crore of bullion and digi-gold sales [1][4]. On an ex-bullion basis, total income hit ₹76,078 crore with ₹8,082 crore EBIT and ₹5,073 crore PAT [4]. Jewellery remains the core profit engine, driving ~88% of revenue and ~89% of segment EBIT [4].

web_blocks.takeaway: Jewellery generates ~90% of revenue and ~89% of operating profit, making Titan's consolidated economics overwhelmingly a branded jewellery compounding engine, supplemented by a high-margin analog watch franchise and rapidly narrowing Emerging losses.

web_blocks.html: Jewellery (~88% of revenue): Titan segments Indian jewellery across five distinct brands. Tanishq serves bridal and festive buyers, while Zoya targets ultra-luxury atelier clients. Mia by Tanishq offers modern daily wear, CaratLane leads omnichannel studded jewellery, and beYon serves lab-grown diamonds [2][11][13]. By September 30, 2026, domestic retail expanded to 875 Tanishq, Mia, Zoya, and beYon stores (with beYon reaching 7 exclusive stores by November 2026) plus 394 CaratLane stores, within a group network of 3,758 outlets (Q2 FY27 business update & ICRA, Nov 25, 2026). Abroad, Titan operates 164 overseas jewellery and eyecare stores across the GCC, North America, and Singapore, including ~122 active Damas GCC showrooms post-restructuring (down from 146 announced at signing after discontinuing monobrand franchises; ICRA, Nov 25, 2026) [3][10].

Concrete example: A family in Bengaluru visits Tanishq to buy a ₹4.5 lakh bridal necklace, exchanging ₹2.0 lakh of old 22-karat gold. The store tests the old gold on a Karatmeter in front of the family and credits 100% of its bullion value [1][17]. Titan books ₹4.5 lakh in revenue, earns 12%–22% making charges, and collects ₹2.5 lakh net cash. It then melts the old gold for reuse, lowering bullion import needs and lifting store traffic.

Watches & Wearables (~6.5% of revenue): This division spans Titan, Edge, Nebula, Raga, Fastrack, Sonata, and Helios stores [2]. In FY26, standalone revenue grew 16% to ₹4,775 crore with ₹775 crore EBIT (16.2% margin), while consolidated segment revenue reached ~₹4,962 crore with ~₹827 crore EBIT (16.7% margin) on premiumization [4][5]. Concrete example: A young professional in Pune buys an ₹18,500 Titan Edge watch at a Helios store. High gross margins on analog designs and Helios multi-brand scale turn a mature category into a 16%+ EBIT cash cow.

EyeCare (~1.0% of revenue): With 800+ Titan Eye+ stores, EyeCare generated ~₹556 crore domestic revenue in FY26 at ~10%–11% EBIT margins [2][4]. Concrete example: A 45-year-old buyer in Jaipur takes a free 20-step eye test at Titan Eye+ and orders ₹6,500 progressive lenses. Prescription glasses are fabricated at Titan's central Chikkaballapur lab, driving repeat loyalty across family members.

Emerging Businesses & TEAL (~2.8% of revenue): Taneira sarees (76 stores), Skinn fragrances (2 standalone stores plus multi-brand distribution), and Irth bags (21 stores) scaled ~29% YoY in FY26 with ₹114–₹123 crore annual EBIT losses [2][4]. Execution improved sharply in Q2 FY27: Emerging total income rose 20.8% YoY to ₹171 crore while the quarterly EBIT loss narrowed 75% YoY to ₹6 crore (versus ₹24 crore in Q2 FY26) on stronger fragrance profitability (Q2 FY27 investor presentation). Meanwhile, subsidiary TEAL supplies precision aerospace and automation components, delivering ₹1,000+ crore revenue and ₹130+ crore EBIT [4].

book_paragraphs: Before you and I look at a single ratio, we need to strip away the myth that Titan is a diversified lifestyle conglomerate. On paper, Titan sells watches, eyeglasses, sarees, perfumes, handbags, aerospace parts, and jewellery. In reality, when we open the audited FY26 ledger and H1 FY27 filings, nearly ₹90 out of every ₹100 of revenue—and roughly ₹89 out of every ₹100 of operating profit—comes from Jewellery, operating across 3,758 total retail stores as of September 2026 (including 164 overseas outlets and ~122 active Damas GCC showrooms post-restructuring).

That concentration is not a flaw; it is the whole point. Titan uses its heritage Watch division (which earned a remarkable 16.2% standalone / 16.7% consolidated EBIT margin in FY26) and its clinical EyeCare chain to keep its brand ubiquitous in every Indian mall and high street, while deploying the bulk of its capital into the far larger, far less organized jewellery market. Just as important, headline Q2 FY27 profit of ₹2,393 crore must be read cleanly: stripping both a ₹671 crore non-cash Damas put-option credit and ₹536 crore of customs-duty inventory gains leaves normalized pre-tax profit of ₹1,793 crore (+17.8% YoY)—solid core compounding rather than a one-off windfall.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE FIVE-TIER JEWELLERY LADDER
book_callouts.text: What impresses me most about Titan's jewellery architecture is how cleanly it segments price points without diluting Tanishq. Zoya serves the ultra-rich, Tanishq owns the Indian bride, Mia captures the salaried woman, CaratLane owns online-to-offline daily diamonds across 394 stores, and beYon (now at 7 exclusive stores) ring-fences lab-grown diamonds with a strict no-exchange rule so synthetic price deflation never touches Tanishq's balance sheet.

book_subsections.title: Walking the Store Floor Across Every Division
paragraphs: Picture a Bengaluru family walking into Tanishq for a ₹4.5 lakh bridal necklace. They do not bring ₹4.5 lakh in cash. They bring 30 grams of inherited family gold. Tanishq tests it on a Karatmeter right in front of them, credits roughly ₹2.3 lakh with zero deduction on Tanishq-origin gold, applies an 11-month Golden Harvest savings balance, and collects the rest by card. That old-gold exchange engine drives nearly half of all festive transactions, turning Indian household gold drawers into Titan's cheapest customer-acquisition channel.

Now walk down the same high street into Helios or Titan World. A buyer skips a ₹2,500 disposable smartwatch and picks up an ₹18,500 Titan Edge Ceramic analog timepiece. That shift toward premium analog watches lifted Watches & Wearables to ~₹4,962 crore consolidated (₹4,775 crore standalone) FY26 revenue and ₹412 crore EBIT in Q2 FY27 alone.

Next door at Titan Eye+, an optometrist runs a standardized 20-step eye exam, sends the prescription to Titan's Chikkaballapur lens lab, and delivers progressive spectacles in 48 hours—generating ₹281 crore in Q2 FY27 sales, up 28% YoY. Behind the scenes, Emerging Businesses (Taneira, Skinn, and Irth) showed tangible operating discipline in Q2 FY27, slashing their quarterly EBIT loss 75% YoY to just ₹6 crore on ₹171 crore of income thanks to profitable fragrances, while precision-engineering subsidiary TEAL quietly builds automated assembly lines for EV and aerospace clients.
